ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit diagram shows a three-node resistor ladder network, with a common wire at the bottom. On the left there is an upward current source, labeled Is, connected to the bottom common node and the upper-left node. The upper-left node has a 1Ω resistor connected to the bottom; between the upper-left node and the middle upper node there is a 2Ω resistor; the middle upper node has a 3Ω resistor connected to the bottom; between the middle upper node and the upper-right node there is a 4Ω resistor; the upper-right node has a 5Ω resistor connected to the bottom. Across the 5Ω resistor is labeled Ux, with polarity upper positive and lower negative. Reasoning: Take the bottom common wire as 0 V. It is known that Ux = 10 V, and Ux is applied across the 5Ω resistor, with the upper end positive, so the upper-right node voltage is 10 V. The 5Ω branch current is 10/5 = 2 A, directed downward. This 2 A at the upper-right node must be supplied by the 4Ω resistor flowing from the middle node to the right node, therefore (V_mid - 10)/4 = 2, obtaining V_mid = 18 V. The downward current through 3Ω at the middle node is 18/3 = 6 A; adding the 2 A through 4Ω to the right, the current flowing into the middle node from the left-side 2Ω resistor should be 8 A. Therefore (V_left - 18)/2 = 8, obtaining V_left = 34 V. The downward current in the left-side 1Ω branch is 34/1 = 34 A, and at the same time the current through 2Ω to the right is 8 A, so the current source needs to provide upward Is = 34 + 8 = 42 A.

method.method_draft: First describe the image-grounded circuit as a three-node resistive ladder fed by an upward current source at the left. Take the bottom rail as 0 V. At the right node, KCL requires 2 A through the 4Ω resistor from the middle node to the right node, so the middle node voltage is 10+2·4=18 V. The 3Ω current is 18/3=6 A downward. At the middle node, the current entering from the 2Ω resistor must supply 6 A down the 3Ω plus 2 A through the 4Ω, so it is 8 A; therefore the left node voltage is 18+8·2=34 V. The 1Ω current is 34/1=34 A, and the current source must supply the 34 A shunt current plus the 8 A through the 2Ω resistor, giving Is=42 A.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a ladder with top-node voltages VA, VB, VC and ground along the bottom. From the text and polarity mark on the image, set VC=Ux=10 V. Write KCL at node C, which has only the 4Ω link to node B and the 5Ω shunt to ground: (VC−VB)/4 + VC/5 = 0, giving VB. Then write KCL at node B: (VB−VA)/2 + VB/3 + (VB−VC)/4 = 0, giving VA. Finally use KCL at node A, where the upward current source injects Is and currents leave through the 1Ω shunt and the 2Ω resistor: Is = VA/1 + (VA−VB)/2. Substituting VC=10 gives VB=18 V, VA=34 V, and Is=42 A, reported as 42.0 A.
